**Read This First**

This document contains everything needed to build the HMS backend (the Laravel REST API, MySQL database, business rules, security, jobs and deployment). Open it, or its Markdown copy, in the hms-backend folder in Cursor. The React screens are described in the separate HMS Frontend document.

**How the two documents are split**

| **Topic**                                      | **In this backend document**    | **In the frontend document**                  |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| **Requirements and roles**                     | Sections 3 to 5 (full)          | Sections 3 to 5 (full, same text)             |
| **Permissions and rules**                      | Sections 8 and 9: enforced here | Sections 8 and 9: mirrored in forms and menus |
| **Workflows, statuses, data model**            | Sections 10 and 11              | Sections 10 and 11                            |
| **Database**                                   | Section 12 (backend only)       | Not included                                  |
| **Architecture and project structure**         | Section 13 (Laravel modules)    | Section 13 (overview only)                    |
| **API contract and authentication**            | Sections 14 and 15              | Sections 14 and 15 (what the client calls)    |
| **Security, audit, notifications, deployment** | Sections 16 to 19 and 24        | Frontend rules in Section 27                  |
| **Screens, routes, UI states**                 | Not included                    | Section 20                                    |
| **Task breakdown**                             | Section 26 (backend tasks)      | Section 26 (frontend tasks)                   |

_Section numbers match the master HMS documentation, so any "see Section N" reference stays valid. Sections that belong only to the other repository are left out, so numbers may skip._

**Working with this document in Cursor**

- Keep this file in hms-backend/docs/. Cursor reads plain text best, so also keep a Markdown copy of it in the same folder and refer to it in prompts with @docs.
- Add the rules below as a project rule file (Cursor reads project rules from the .cursor/rules folder, or an older .cursorrules file). Check Cursor's current documentation for the exact file format your version uses.
- Work one task at a time using the Task IDs in Section 26 (for example P1-T2). Give Cursor the task, the sections to follow, and ask for tests first.
- Never ask Cursor to build a whole phase in one prompt; review each task, run the tests, then commit.

**Suggested project rule file**

```
---
description: HMS backend conventions
alwaysApply: true
---
- Stack: Laravel 11, PHP 8.2+, MySQL 8, Sanctum SPA cookie auth, Redis queue, Pest tests.
- Architecture: modular monolith in app/Modules/<Module>. Controllers are thin;
  business rules live in Service classes inside DB transactions.
- Every endpoint needs: Form Request, permission check (default deny), API Resource, OpenAPI entry.
- Money is DECIMAL(12,2) only. Store times in UTC. Never hard-delete clinical or financial data.
- Never accept role, status, paid amount or ownership fields from the client.
- Errors: domain exceptions with a code and HTTP status; JSON shape from Section 14.
- Write failing tests first: rules, status transitions, each role (allowed and forbidden), constraints.
- Source of truth: docs/ - permissions Section 8, rules Section 9, statuses Section 10,
  tables Section 12, endpoints Section 14, build order Section 26.
```

**Prompt template for one task**

```
Implement task P1-T2 (Sanctum authentication) from @docs.
Follow Section 8 (permissions), Section 9 (rules) and Section 14 (API).
Write the failing tests first, then the migration, model, policy, service,
request, controller, resource and route. Update openapi.yaml.
Stop and list anything in the docs that is unclear before you write code.
```

**3\. Vision, goals and scope**

HMS digitises one hospital's patient journey from registration to billing, so staff stop using paper and spreadsheets and patients can book, pay and view their records online.

**Goals (targets are assumptions; confirm them)**

- Register a new patient in under 2 minutes.
- A patient books and pays for an appointment in under 3 minutes from login.
- Zero double-booked doctor slots, enforced by the database, not only by code.
- Every clinical change and every payment is traceable to a user and a time.
- 95% of API responses under 500 ms and pages usable in under 1.5 s with 50 concurrent users.

**Scope**

| **Priority**  | **Included**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| MVP (Must)    | Authentication, users, roles and permissions; patients; doctors and schedules; appointments with fee payment, reschedule, cancel, check-in; consultations, vitals, diagnoses, prescriptions; medical records; services, invoices, payments, refunds, expenses; wards, beds, admission and discharge; role dashboards and core reports; email notifications; audit logs; patient portal; settings |
| Should (v1.1) | Lab tests and results; PDF invoices and prescriptions; in-app notification bell; bed transfers; automatic no-show; SMS or WhatsApp reminders; online refund automation                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Later         | Pharmacy stock and dispensing; insurance and claims; multi-branch; HR and payroll; telemedicine; mobile app; patient merge tool; barcode patient cards; HL7 or FHIR integration                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Out of scope  | Imaging (PACS), clinical decision support, government reporting integrations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

**Working assumptions**

- One hospital, one branch, one currency (set in Settings), one time zone.
- Walk-in patients are handled as same-day appointments created by the receptionist.
- The online payment gateway is not chosen yet; it sits behind a payment provider interface so any gateway can be plugged in (OQ-02).
- The user interface is English first but written so translations can be added.

**4\. Actors and roles**

HMS has five human roles, each with its own panel in the React app, plus four system actors that act without a person.

| **Actor**              | **Type** | **Logs in**  | **Main responsibilities**                                                                                                                                                      | **Lands on after login**            |
| ---------------------- | -------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- |
| Admin                  | Human    | Yes          | Manages users, roles, doctors, master data (departments, wards, beds, services), settings; sees everything; reads audit logs; approves refunds and large discounts             | Admin dashboard                     |
| Receptionist           | Human    | Yes          | Registers patients, books and reschedules appointments for patients, takes fee at the counter, checks patients in, admits and discharges, creates bills, views doctors         | Reception dashboard (today's queue) |
| Doctor                 | Human    | Yes          | Manages own availability, sees own appointments and patients, runs consultations, records vitals and diagnoses, writes prescriptions and medical records, summarises discharge | Doctor dashboard (today's queue)    |
| Accountant             | Human    | Yes          | Manages price list, invoices, payments and refunds, expenses, financial reports                                                                                                | Finance dashboard                   |
| Patient                | Human    | Yes (portal) | Registers and logs in, views doctors, books and pays for appointments, views prescriptions, medical record and bills                                                           | Patient home                        |
| Scheduler              | System   | No           | Expires unpaid slot holds, sends reminders, marks no-shows, runs backups and clean-up                                                                                          | \-                                  |
| Payment gateway        | System   | No           | Calls a signed webhook to confirm or fail online payments                                                                                                                      | \-                                  |
| Email and SMS provider | System   | No           | Delivers notifications sent from the queue                                                                                                                                     | \-                                  |
| Queue worker           | System   | No           | Runs notification, report and PDF jobs in the background                                                                                                                       | \-                                  |

**Login user versus business entity**

- The users table holds everyone who can log in. Patients and doctors are business entities with their own tables.
- A doctor always has exactly one user (doctors.user_id is required). A patient may have none, or one portal account (patients.user_id is nullable).
- A user has one or more roles; the interface and API check permissions (Section 8), never role names.
- The first Admin is created by a database seeder; there is no public Admin registration.

**6\. Non-functional requirements**

These targets are assumptions for a single hospital; change the numbers here first if your situation differs.

| **Category**        | **Requirement**                                                                                                        | **Target**                                                    |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Performance         | API response time for list and read endpoints                                                                          | 95% under 500 ms; pages usable under 1.5 s                    |
| Capacity            | Concurrent users; data volume in 3 years                                                                               | 50 concurrent; about 20,000 patients and 200,000 appointments |
| Scalability         | Every list endpoint is paginated (default 25, max 100); no unbounded queries                                           | Mandatory                                                     |
| Availability        | Monthly uptime; maintenance window                                                                                     | 99.5%; off-hours only                                         |
| Security            | HTTPS everywhere, hashed passwords, permission checks on every endpoint, rate limiting                                 | Section 16                                                    |
| Privacy             | Doctors see only patients they treat; every view of a clinical record is logged                                        | Section 8 and 18                                              |
| Auditability        | Who created, changed or viewed clinical and financial records, with old and new values                                 | Section 18                                                    |
| Backup and recovery | Daily database backup kept 30 days, copy stored off-server, restore tested monthly                                     | Data loss up to 24 h (RPO), recovery within 4 h (RTO)         |
| Data retention      | Medical and financial records are never hard-deleted; retention period set by local law                                | Confirm in OQ-07                                              |
| Usability           | Desktop-first, usable on tablet and phone for the patient portal; clear empty, loading, error and no-permission states | Section 20                                                    |
| Compatibility       | Latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari                                                                | Mandatory                                                     |
| Maintainability     | PSR-12 and Laravel Pint on the backend; ESLint and Prettier on the frontend; CI runs tests on every pull request       | Mandatory                                                     |
| Localisation        | Currency, time zone and date format come from Settings; text is kept in translation files                              | Mandatory                                                     |
| Reliability         | Payments are idempotent; background jobs retry 3 times with backoff; failed jobs are visible                           | Mandatory                                                     |

**8\. Roles and permissions**

Access is decided by permissions named resource.action, bundled into roles, then narrowed by scope and by the access rules below; the backend enforces all of it and the React app only hides what the user cannot use.

**Permission matrix**

Scope values: all = every record; own = records belonging to the logged-in user; assigned = records of patients the doctor treats (see AR-02); basic = limited fields only; dash = no access.

| **Permission**                            | **Admin**            | **Receptionist** | **Doctor**                  | **Accountant** | **Patient**         |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------- |
| users.view / create / update / deactivate | all                  | \-               | \-                          | \-             | \-                  |
| roles.view / manage                       | all                  | \-               | \-                          | \-             | \-                  |
| patients.view                             | all                  | all              | assigned                    | basic          | own                 |
| patients.search                           | all                  | all              | all (basic)                 | basic          | \-                  |
| patients.create                           | all                  | all              | \-                          | \-             | self-register       |
| patients.update                           | all                  | all              | \-                          | \-             | own (contact only)  |
| patients.deactivate                       | all                  | \-               | \-                          | \-             | \-                  |
| doctors.view                              | all                  | all              | all                         | basic          | all (public fields) |
| doctors.create / update / deactivate      | all                  | \-               | \-                          | \-             | \-                  |
| schedules.view                            | all                  | all              | own                         | \-             | all (free slots)    |
| schedules.manage                          | all                  | \-               | own                         | \-             | \-                  |
| appointments.view                         | all                  | all              | own                         | basic          | own                 |
| appointments.create                       | all                  | all              | \-                          | \-             | own                 |
| appointments.reschedule                   | all                  | all              | \-                          | \-             | own (24 h rule)     |

| consultations.view                        | all (read)           | \-               | own and assigned            | \-             | own (completed)     |
| consultations.create / update / complete  | \-                   | \-               | own                         | \-             | \-                  |
| prescriptions.view                        | all (read)           | \-               | own and assigned            | \-             | own                 |
| prescriptions.create / cancel             | \-                   | \-               | own                         | \-             | \-                  |
| medical_records.view                      | all (read)           | \-               | assigned                    | \-             | own                 |
| medical_records.create / update           | \-                   | \-               | assigned                    | \-             | \-                  |

Permission names are seeded from this table; a role is created by attaching permissions, so adding a role later needs no code change.

**Access rules beyond roles**

| **ID**                   | **Rule**                                                                                                                 | **Example**                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AR-01 Ownership          | A patient reaches only records linked to their own patient id                                                            | A patient cannot open another patient's invoice by changing the id in the URL                    |
| AR-02 Care relationship  | A doctor reaches a patient's clinical data only if they have an appointment, consultation or admission with that patient | Doctor A cannot browse patients of Doctor B                                                      |
| AR-03 Break-glass        | A doctor or Admin may open any patient record by entering a reason; the access is logged and reviewed                    | Emergency treatment of an unknown patient                                                        |
| AR-04 State-based        | Edits depend on status                                                                                                   | Completed consultation and issued invoice are locked                                             |
| AR-05 Time-based         | Patient cancel or reschedule only until the cut-off                                                                      | 24 hours before the slot                                                                         |
| AR-06 Field-level        | Some fields are hidden by role                                                                                           | Accountant sees patient name and number, not diagnoses; receptionist does not see clinical notes |
| AR-07 Approval           | Large actions need a second person                                                                                       | Refund above the limit and discount above the limit need Admin approval                          |
| AR-08 Separation of duty | The requester cannot approve their own request                                                                           | An Accountant cannot approve their own refund                                                    |
| AR-09 Default deny       | No permission means no access, including new endpoints                                                                   | A new route without a policy returns 403                                                         |
| AR-10 Last Admin         | The last active Admin cannot be deactivated or lose the role                                                             | Prevents locking everyone out                                                                    |

**9\. Business rules**

These rules are the heart of the system: each one is a single sentence with exact numbers, lives in a service class (not in a controller or the UI), and where possible is also enforced by a database constraint. Numbers marked (setting) are editable in Settings.

**Patients and users**

| **ID**    | **Rule**                                                                                                                                                         | **Enforced at**        |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| BR-PAT-01 | The patient number is generated by the system as P-YYYY-NNNNNN, is unique, never reused and never editable                                                       | Service + unique index |
| BR-PAT-02 | Registration warns when another patient has the same phone and date of birth, or the same full name and date of birth; the receptionist must confirm to continue | Service                |
| BR-PAT-03 | A patient is never hard-deleted; deactivation hides them from booking only                                                                                       | Service + soft delete  |
| BR-PAT-04 | A patient under 18 needs a guardian name and phone                                                                                                               | Form request           |
| BR-USR-01 | Email is unique; a doctor login cannot exist without a doctor profile                                                                                            | Unique index + service |
| BR-USR-02 | The last active Admin cannot be deactivated or lose the Admin role                                                                                               | Service                |
| BR-USR-03 | Passwords have at least 10 characters; 5 failed logins lock the account for 15 minutes (setting)                                                                 | Auth service           |

**Appointments**

| **ID**    | **Rule**                                                                                                                                                                                            | **Enforced at**                                             |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| BR-APT-01 | A doctor has at most one active appointment for the same date and start time; cancelled, expired and no-show rows free the slot                                                                     | DB unique index on (doctor_id, date, start_time, is_active) |
| BR-APT-02 | A slot must fall inside the doctor's weekly schedule, on a slot boundary, in the future, and not on a leave day                                                                                     | Slot service                                                |
| BR-APT-03 | A new booking is pending_payment and holds the slot for 10 minutes (setting); it becomes scheduled when the consultation fee is paid online or recorded at the counter; unpaid holds become expired | Booking service + scheduler                                 |
| BR-APT-04 | A patient may have at most 3 active future appointments and only one per doctor per day                                                                                                             | Booking service                                             |
| BR-APT-05 | A patient can cancel or reschedule until 24 hours before the start (setting); receptionist and Admin can do it any time with a reason                                                               | Appointment service                                         |
| BR-APT-06 | Refund on patient cancellation: 100% if 24 hours or more before the start, 50% if between 2 and 24 hours, 0% if under 2 hours; cancellation by the hospital or doctor is always 100% (settings)     | Refund calculator                                           |
| BR-APT-07 | Check-in is allowed only on the appointment date and only from scheduled; it assigns the next token number for that doctor and day                                                                  | Appointment service                                         |
| BR-APT-08 | A scheduled appointment not checked in 30 minutes after its end time becomes no_show and its fee is not refunded (setting)                                                                          | Scheduler                                                   |
| BR-APT-09 | Only a checked_in appointment can start a consultation                                                                                                                                              | Consultation service                                        |
| BR-APT-10 | Rescheduling creates a new appointment linked to the old one; the old one becomes cancelled with reason rescheduled and its payment moves to the new one                                            | Appointment service                                         |

**Consultations and prescriptions**

| **ID**    | **Rule**                                                                                                                                             | **Enforced at**                |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| BR-CON-01 | An appointment has zero or one consultation                                                                                                          | Unique index on appointment_id |
| BR-CON-02 | Only the assigned doctor can create, edit or complete the consultation                                                                               | Policy                         |
| BR-CON-03 | Starting a consultation moves the appointment to in_consultation; completing it moves the appointment to completed                                   | Consultation service           |
| BR-CON-04 | A completed consultation is locked; corrections are addenda that keep the original text                                                              | Service                        |
| BR-CON-05 | A prescription needs a consultation that is in_progress, or completed less than 24 hours ago, by the same doctor                                     | Prescription service           |
| BR-CON-06 | Each prescription item needs a medicine, dose, frequency and duration in days                                                                        | Form request                   |
| BR-CON-07 | Known allergies of the patient are shown before a medicine is added and a warning needs acknowledgment when a medicine name matches an allergy entry | UI + service                   |

**Billing, payments and expenses**

| **ID**    | **Rule**                                                                                                                                                                                               | **Enforced at**                |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| BR-BIL-01 | Invoice numbers are INV-YYYY-NNNNNN, sequential, generated inside a database transaction using a locked counter row                                                                                    | Sequence service               |
| BR-BIL-02 | Invoice total = sum of (quantity x unit price) - discount + tax, rounded to 2 decimals; money is DECIMAL(12,2)                                                                                         | Invoice calculator             |
| BR-BIL-03 | Only draft invoices are editable; issued, partially_paid and paid invoices change only through payments, cancellation or a new invoice                                                                 | Policy + service               |
| BR-BIL-04 | Status follows payments: nothing paid is issued, some paid is partially_paid, paid amount equal to total is paid; paid amount can never exceed the total                                               | Payment service                |
| BR-BIL-05 | A discount above 10% of the invoice (setting) needs Admin approval                                                                                                                                     | Invoice service                |
| BR-BIL-06 | An invoice with payments can be cancelled only after all payments are refunded                                                                                                                         | Invoice service                |
| BR-BIL-07 | A refund is a separate payment row of type refund linked to the original, never larger than the amount paid; refunds above the limit (setting) need Admin approval by someone other than the requester | Payment service                |
| BR-BIL-08 | The consultation-fee invoice is created at booking with a snapshot of the doctor's fee; later fee changes do not touch existing invoices                                                               | Booking service                |
| BR-BIL-09 | Online payments are confirmed only by a verified, signed gateway webhook and are idempotent on the gateway reference                                                                                   | Webhook handler + unique index |
| BR-BIL-10 | Expenses are never deleted; they are voided with a reason                                                                                                                                              | Service                        |

**Admissions**

| **ID**    | **Rule**                                                                                                                                              | **Enforced at**                           |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| BR-ADM-01 | A bed has at most one active admission and a patient at most one active admission                                                                     | DB unique indexes on nullable active keys |
| BR-ADM-02 | Only a bed with status available can be assigned; assigning sets it to occupied; discharge or transfer sets it back to available                      | Admission service                         |
| BR-ADM-03 | The admission number is generated as ADM-YYYY-NNNNNN                                                                                                  | Sequence service                          |
| BR-ADM-04 | Discharge needs a discharge summary (diagnosis, condition, instructions) from the admitting doctor and a discharge time not before the admission time | Admission service                         |
| BR-ADM-05 | On discharge the system adds bed charges = number of days (rounded up, minimum 1) x ward daily rate to the admission invoice                          | Admission service                         |
| BR-ADM-06 | Discharge is blocked while the admission invoice has an outstanding balance unless an Admin overrides with a reason (setting: clearance required)     | Admission service                         |

**10\. Business workflows and status lifecycles**

Every visit follows one path from registration to billing, every record moves through a fixed set of statuses, and each flow below lists what happens when something goes wrong.

![HMS diagram](data:image/png;base64,)

patient journey · 9 steps, 1 decision

The fee must be paid before a slot is confirmed; admission is the only branch that leaves the normal visit path.

**Flows and their failure paths**

| **Flow**                          | **Actors**               | **Main steps**                                                                                                                               | **What can go wrong and what the system does**                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F-01 Register patient             | Receptionist             | Search first, enter details, system warns on duplicates, save, patient number generated                                                      | Duplicate found: warn and require confirmation. Invalid data: 422 with field messages                                                                            |
| F-02 Book appointment (portal)    | Patient                  | Pick doctor, date, free slot and reason; slot held 10 minutes and fee invoice created; pay online; appointment becomes scheduled; email sent | Slot taken: 409 and slots refresh. Payment fails or times out: hold expires, status expired. Payment succeeds but the page closes: the webhook still confirms it |
| F-03 Book appointment (reception) | Receptionist             | Select patient, doctor, slot and reason; take payment online or cash; appointment scheduled                                                  | Same as F-02; a cash payment must create a payment row, so the invoice and the cash drawer agree                                                                 |
| F-04 Cancel or reschedule         | Patient, Receptionist    | Request, rules checked, refund calculated, status and slot updated, notification sent                                                        | After the cut-off the patient is blocked and the receptionist continues with a reason. Refund fails at the gateway: refund stays pending and is retried          |
| F-05 Check-in and consultation    | Receptionist, Doctor     | Check in and token; doctor starts the consultation; vitals, symptoms, diagnoses, plan; prescription; complete                                | Not scheduled for today: blocked. Another doctor opens it: 403. Doctor leaves mid-way: draft is saved and the status stays in_consultation                       |
| F-06 Billing and payment          | Receptionist, Accountant | Create invoice from services with tax and discount; issue; record payments; status follows the paid amount                                   | Discount above the limit waits for Admin. Overpayment: 422. Double click: the idempotency key returns the first result                                           |
| F-07 Refund                       | Accountant, Admin        | Request with reason; Admin approves above the limit; refund row created; invoice status updated                                              | Approver is the requester: blocked. Refund larger than the amount paid: 422                                                                                      |
| F-08 Admission and discharge      | Receptionist, Doctor     | Select patient, doctor, ward, bed; admit; treat; doctor writes the summary; clear the balance; discharge; bed charges added; bed freed       | Bed taken: 409. Patient already admitted: 409. Balance outstanding: blocked unless Admin overrides with a reason                                                 |
| F-09 Patient portal onboarding    | Patient                  | Register, verify email, link to the patient record by number and date of birth                                                               | Wrong details: neutral failure with attempts limited. No record yet: the receptionist registers the patient first                                                |
| F-10 Scheduled jobs               | System                   | Expire holds, send reminders, mark no-shows, back up                                                                                         | Job fails: retried 3 times, then listed in failed jobs and alerted                                                                                               |

**Status lifecycles**

![HMS diagram](data:image/png;base64,)

status lifecycles · appointment, invoice, admission

Statuses are stored as these exact strings; the table says who may trigger each move and what else happens.

| **Record**   | **From**                 | **Event**                       | **To**          | **Who**                           | **Condition and side effects**                       |
| ------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Appointment  | pending_payment          | Fee paid                        | scheduled       | System or receptionist            | Payment row exists; confirmation email               |
| Appointment  | pending_payment          | Hold ends                       | expired         | Scheduler                         | Slot becomes free                                    |
| Appointment  | scheduled                | Cancel                          | cancelled       | Patient, Receptionist, Admin      | Cut-off and refund rules BR-APT-05 and 06            |
| Appointment  | scheduled                | Not checked in 30 min after end | no_show         | Scheduler, Receptionist           | No refund                                            |
| Appointment  | scheduled                | Check-in                        | checked_in      | Receptionist                      | Same day only; token assigned                        |
| Appointment  | checked_in               | Start consultation              | in_consultation | Doctor                            | Consultation created                                 |
| Appointment  | in_consultation          | Complete consultation           | completed       | Doctor                            | Consultation locked                                  |
| Consultation | in_progress              | Complete                        | completed       | Assigned doctor                   | Later changes are addenda                            |
| Invoice      | draft                    | Issue                           | issued          | Creator                           | Number and amounts locked                            |
| Invoice      | issued                   | Part payment                    | partially_paid  | Cashier                           | Paid amount below total                              |
| Invoice      | issued or partially_paid | Full payment                    | paid            | Cashier, webhook                  | Paid amount equals total                             |
| Invoice      | draft or issued          | Cancel                          | cancelled       | Accountant, Admin                 | Only while nothing is paid                           |
| Admission    | requested                | Admit                           | admitted        | Receptionist                      | Bed becomes occupied                                 |
| Admission    | admitted                 | Discharge                       | discharged      | Receptionist after doctor summary | Bed freed; bed charges added; balance rule BR-ADM-06 |
| Admission    | requested or admitted    | Cancel                          | cancelled       | Receptionist, Admin               | Bed freed                                            |

**12\. Database design**

The MySQL 8 schema has about 45 tables (including Laravel's own) in 6 groups; the rules that can be constraints are constraints, so a coding bug cannot double-book a slot or overpay an invoice.

**Conventions**

- Tables are plural snake_case; foreign keys are singular_table_id; pivot tables are alphabetical (role_user).
- Every table has id (BIGINT unsigned, auto-increment), created_at and updated_at. Business tables also have created_by and updated_by (user ids). Patients, doctors, invoices and users use soft deletes.
- Foreign keys always state ON DELETE: RESTRICT by default, CASCADE only for true children (invoice_items, prescription_items).
- Money is DECIMAL(12,2). Dates without time use DATE, instants use DATETIME in UTC. Statuses are VARCHAR(20) matching Section 10 exactly (PHP backed enums on the Laravel side).
- Uniqueness for rules uses a nullable flag column (is_active = 1 or NULL): MySQL treats NULLs as different, so finished rows release the unique key.
- Every list query is backed by an index in the tables below; add an index only for a named query.

**Access and system**

| **Table**                                                                         | **Key columns**                                                                                                             | **Constraints and indexes**                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| users                                                                             | name, email, password, phone, is_active, email_verified_at, last_login_at, failed_login_count, locked_until, remember_token | Unique email; index is_active; soft deletes                                                                                        |
| roles                                                                             | name (slug), label, is_system                                                                                               | Unique name                                                                                                                        |
| permissions                                                                       | name (resource.action), group                                                                                               | Unique name                                                                                                                        |
| role_user                                                                         | user_id, role_id                                                                                                            | Primary key (user_id, role_id)                                                                                                     |
| permission_role                                                                   | permission_id, role_id                                                                                                      | Primary key (permission_id, role_id)                                                                                               |
| personal_access_tokens, password_reset_tokens, sessions, jobs, failed_jobs, cache | Laravel and Sanctum defaults                                                                                                | As generated by Laravel                                                                                                            |
| settings                                                                          | key, value (JSON), group                                                                                                    | Unique key                                                                                                                         |
| sequences                                                                         | name, year, last_number                                                                                                     | Unique (name, year); row locked with SELECT FOR UPDATE when generating numbers                                                     |
| audit_logs                                                                        | user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, old_values (JSON), new_values (JSON), reason, ip_address, user_agent, created_at   | Indexes (entity_type, entity_id), (user_id, created_at), (created_at); no updated_at; app database user has INSERT and SELECT only |
| notifications                                                                     | Laravel database notification columns (type, notifiable, data, read_at)                                                     | Index (notifiable_type, notifiable_id, read_at)                                                                                    |

**Key queries the indexes must serve**

1. Free slots for a doctor on a date: schedules + leaves + active appointments by (doctor_id, appointment_date).
2. Today's queue for a doctor: appointments by (doctor_id, appointment_date, status), ordered by token.
3. Patient search by number, phone, name or national ID.
4. Patient history: appointments, invoices, prescriptions, admissions by patient_id.
5. Expired holds: appointments where status is pending_payment and hold_expires_at is past.
6. Outstanding invoices: invoices by status and issued_at, with balance.
7. Collections by day and method: payments by (paid_at, method).
8. Bed availability by ward: beds by (ward_id, status).
9. Audit search by entity and by user and date.
10. Doctor revenue and consultation counts by date range.

**Migration, seed and backup plan**

- One migration per table, in dependency order, each reversible; never edit a migration that has run in staging or production, add a new one.
- Seeders: roles, permissions and role-permission links; the first Admin; default settings; departments, specializations; a demo hospital dataset for local and staging only.
- Factories exist for every model so tests build realistic data.
- Back up with mysqldump or a managed snapshot daily plus binary logs, copy off-server, and test a restore each month.

**13\. System architecture and project structure**

HMS is a modular monolith: one Laravel API with clear module boundaries, one React app in its own repository, one MySQL database, and a queue for slow work; microservices are not needed for a single hospital.

![HMS diagram](data:image/png;base64,)

system architecture · 2 repositories, 1 API, 1 database

Every request passes middleware, a thin controller, then a service where the business rules and the transaction live; slow work leaves through events and the queue.

**Architecture decisions (record each as an ADR)**

| **ADR** | **Decision**                                                                                              | **Reason**                                                                                     |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ADR-001 | Modular monolith, not microservices                                                                       | Small team, one hospital, one deployable, fastest delivery; split later only for a proven need |
| ADR-002 | Two repositories: hms-backend and hms-frontend, API versioned under /api/v1, OpenAPI file as the contract | Independent deploys and teams; frontend can work against a mock                                |
| ADR-003 | Cookie-based Sanctum authentication on one parent domain (Section 15)                                     | Keeps tokens away from JavaScript                                                              |
| ADR-004 | One database for one hospital; add branch_id later if OQ-01 changes                                       | Avoids multi-tenant cost that is not needed now                                                |
| ADR-005 | Slot uniqueness and bed occupancy enforced by unique indexes with nullable active flags                   | A coding bug cannot double-book                                                                |
| ADR-006 | Payments behind a provider interface with idempotency keys and signed webhooks                            | Gateway can change; no double charges                                                          |
| ADR-007 | Soft delete, status changes and audit log instead of hard deletes                                         | Medical and financial history must survive                                                     |

**Layer rules**

- Controllers contain no business logic: authorise, call one service method, return a Resource.
- Form Requests validate input and shape; services own the business rules and wrap changes in a transaction.
- Models hold relationships, scopes and casts; Policies hold permission and access rules; Enums hold statuses.
- Events are dispatched after commit; listeners create notifications and audit entries; jobs run on the queue.
- No repository layer: Eloquent is enough for this size. Add one only where a query is reused and complex.
- A module may call another module's service, never write to its tables directly; cross-module reactions use events.

**Backend structure (hms-backend)**

```
hms-backend/
  app/
    Modules/
      Auth/  Access/  Patients/  Doctors/  Appointments/  Consultations/
      Prescriptions/  Billing/  Expenses/  Admissions/  Notifications/  Reports/  Lab/
        Http/Controllers  Http/Requests  Http/Resources
        Models  Policies  Services  Enums  Events  Listeners  Jobs  Notifications
    Shared/   Audit/  Sequences/  Money/  Exceptions/  Support/
  routes/api/v1/     one route file per module
  database/          migrations/  seeders/  factories/
  tests/             Unit/  Feature/  (mirrors the modules)
  docs/              openapi.yaml and this documentation
```

The frontend structure is in Section 20.

**14\. API specification**

The API is REST over JSON under /api/v1; write the OpenAPI file from this section before coding each module so the React team can build against a mock while the backend is implemented.

**Conventions**

| **Item**                 | **Convention**                                                                                               |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Base URL and versioning  | <https://api.example-hospital.com/api/v1> (version in the path)                                              |
| Format                   | JSON in and out; dates as ISO 8601 UTC; money as strings with 2 decimals (for example 1500.00)               |
| Success                  | Single record: { data: {...} }. List: { data: \[...\], meta: { page, per_page, total, last_page } }          |
| Error                    | { error: { code: SLOT_TAKEN, message: Human readable text, fields: { field: \[messages\] }, request_id } }   |
| Pagination, sort, filter | ?page=2&per_page=25&sort=-created_at&filter\[status\]=scheduled&q=search text                                |
| Authentication           | Every endpoint except those marked public needs a logged-in user (Section 15)                                |
| Authorization            | Each endpoint names its permission; a missing permission returns 403                                         |
| Idempotency              | Payment and booking POSTs accept an Idempotency-Key header; repeating the same key returns the first result  |
| Rate limits              | Login 5 per minute per account and IP; public endpoints 30 per minute; authenticated 120 per minute per user |
| Status codes             | 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No content, 401, 403, 404, 409 state conflict, 422 validation, 429, 500             |
